THE FIXTURE COULD NOT BE IMPORTED, so the plan's documented fallback is what shipped. `CLAUDE_SESSION_LIMIT` is declared `const` (not `export const`) at seat-exit-classifier.test.ts:37. LIMIT_LINE therefore carries a COPY of :49, and `readFixtureLimitLine(root)` reads that source, pulls the `line: "..."` literal out of the CLAUDE_SESSION_LIMIT declaration with a regex, JSON.parses it, and the first arm asserts byte equality against LIMIT_LINE. A fixture edit, a fixture rename or a fixture move all red that arm instead of leaving a stale copy passing. The literal is JSON.parsed rather than string-compared because the fixture writes the MIDDLE DOT as the escape `\u00B7` on purpose (its header, :22-23).

FOUR DEVIATIONS FROM THE STEP TEXT, each measured, none of them optional:

(1) `process.stderr.write(...) ; process.exit(1)` WOULD HAVE BEEN A FLAKE, so the double writes with `require("node:fs").writeSync(2, ...)`. On Windows a write to a PIPE is asynchronous, and `process.exit` is free to discard whatever is still buffered - which is the one line this whole journey turns on. writeSync(2) is flushed before exit by construction. The double's dir has no package.json above it in TEMP, so a `.js` there is CommonJS and `require` is available.

(2) The .cmd and .sh call node by ABSOLUTE PATH (`process.execPath`), not by the bare name. `agent-spawn-environment.ts:52-61` hands a seat a FILTERED environment - only RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS plus the provider prefixes survive, and every MOE_* key is stripped. PATH/PATHEXT/COMSPEC/SYSTEMROOT are on that roster today, so a bare `node` would resolve; pinning the executable makes the double independent of a roster this row does not own. The step's `%~dp0seat-double.js` is unchanged and is still asserted.

(3) `seatDoubleFiles` returns `bytes` as the STRING written, not a Uint8Array. The three files are text and the arms compare text; the one place bytes actually matter - what the seat's stderr carried - is compared as a Buffer against `Buffer.concat([Buffer.from(LIMIT_LINE, "utf8"), Buffer.from("\n")])` in the process arm.

(4) NEW EXPORT `resolveLaneScratch(lane)`, because step 3's premise is wrong: `DaemonLane` (daemon-ports.ts:222-251) does NOT carry `storePath`, so "derive it from lane.storePath's dirname" cannot be written. It reconstructs the LaneScratch by scanning tmpdir() for the one `moe-e2e-daemon-*` entry whose suffix LOWERCASES to the tag in `lane.projectId` (createLaneScratch:93 lowercases the tag, so rejoining it would be wrong on a case-sensitive filesystem), then refuses (null) unless that directory holds store.sqlite AND node-specs/node.json AND that spec names THIS lane's nodeRef. A wrong pick therefore fails loudly instead of pointing the wrapper at another run's board. This keeps the shared daemon-ports.ts untouched - no field added to a returned shape that other specs read (global rail 19).

THE EIGHT ARMS, and what each would miss if it were dropped:
- fixture equality + "exactly one non-ASCII code point, and it is 0xB7" (spelled by CODE POINT so this file stays ASCII and cannot itself be mangled by a console).
- the generated .js carries `\u00b7` as an ESCAPE and is ASCII-only end to end.
- THE PROCESS ARM: `spawnSync(process.execPath, [jsPath])` -> status 1 and stderr byte-equal to the line plus one LF, stdout empty. This is the only assertion that can see what the STREAM carried; every source assertion above it is blind to it. The one process this file spawns.
- the double ignores the spawner's own flags: re-run with `-p --setting-sources "" --mcp-config <absent>` appended and the same status 1 / same bytes. `node -p` would have evaluated an expression instead, which is exactly why a `.cmd`/`.sh` wrapper exists rather than MOE_AGENT_COMMAND=node.
- three files written, `.cmd` starts `@echo off\r\n` (cmd.exe reads CRLF) and contains `%~dp0seat-double.js`, `.sh` starts `#!/bin/sh\n` and contains `"$(dirname "$0")/seat-double.js"`; `command` is the .cmd on win32 and the .sh (mode & 0o111 nonzero) elsewhere.
- wrapperEnv: the four knobs by VALUE, the three inherited store/spec/project keys by value against the real LaneScratch, and the ADDED

(2) THE EVIDENCE LINE LOST THE PIDS ON EVERY RED RUN. `evidence.push(daemonPid, seedPid)` sat AFTER the try/finally, so a failing body skipped it and the record for the run a person most needs to read was the one missing its process identities. Do NOT re-derive or re-word any of them; import the formatters if you need to build an expectation for a DYNAMIC fixture, but spell the literal when you are pinning the wording.

THE FOUR SURFACES A PAUSED SHELL SHOWS, in the order a person meets them:

1. cr.shell.paused (3b's, shell status strip, shell/status-strip.tsx:114) - text is `pauseWords(paused)`:
   `Agents paused: <provider> limit, resumes <when>`

2. cr.sessions.paused (MINE, Seats panel, ops/activity-screens.tsx:129) - text is `pauseSeatWords(paused)`:
   `Agents paused: <provider> limit, resumes <when> - last line from the seat: <lastLine>`
   Renders inside the SESSIONS branch, ABOVE the count line, so it appears even when NO agent seat is live and even when nothing at all is live (that arm exists and is drill-proven). An empty or whitespace-only lastLine renders the literal `(no output)`, never a sentence trailing off after the colon. Absent when the pause is null/unknown.

3. cr.kanban.next (MINE, board header, board/board-header.tsx NextStep) - while the goal's stage is WORKING and a pause is known:
   label: `Waiting for the provider limit to reset at <when>`
   detail (cr.kanban has no detail testid; the strip's is cr.goalstatus.detail): `The <provider> seat hit its limit on <workItemId>; the wrapper staffs again at <resetAt>.`
   NOTE the detail uses the RAW `resetAt`, the label uses the LOCALE-FORMATTED `<when>`. That asymmetry is deliberate (the detail is the daemon's own instant, quotable; the label is for reading).

4. cr.goalstatus.next / cr.goalstatus.detail (MINE, goals/goal-status-strip.tsx) - the SAME two sentences as (3); the strip and the board header both render `status.next` from one `deriveGoalStatus` call.

`<when>` IS NOT A CONSTANT. It is `pauseResetWords(paused)` from v2/shell/pause-context.tsx: `Date.parse(resetAt)` NaN -> the RAW resetAt string, else `new Date(at).toLocaleString()` - the VIEWER'S locale, so a hard-coded "9/3/2026, 2:30:00 PM" will red on a box with different locale settings. In an assertion, write `` `... ${new Date(FIXTURE.resetAt).toLocaleString()}` `` (spell the surrounding words as literals; only share the toLocaleString call). Do NOT call `pauseWords`/`pauseSeatWords`/`pauseResetWords` to BUILD a wording expectation - that passes for whatever they return and voids your own coverage.

So a journey that pauses the provider and then expects EVERY goal card to say "Waiting for the provider limit..." is asserting the wrong thing. Four stages are pinned against this in goal-status.test.tsx ("leaves every stage but WORKING alone while the provider is paused").

- A pause raised on ANOTHER goal's work item still changes THIS goal's WORKING next-step. One wrapper, one provider, so every WORKING goal is genuinely waiting; the detail names the offending workItemId so a person can tell.
- A WORKING goal with ZERO claimed nodes still says "Waiting for the provider limit..." - correct, nothing will be staffed until the reset.
- A `resetAt` already in the past keeps rendering until the next poll answers null. The daemon's clock owns expiry; the client never invents it.
